items.summary:

items.title: New guidance on IMDG Code changes for vehicles and batteries
items.summary:
We have added guidance on changes to the International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code. A member login is required to read the guidance.
The article outlines what Amendment 43-26 means for vehicle shipments and battery cargoes, helping members identify areas to review ahead of implementation.

items.summary: BIMCO has co-sponsored a proposal to the International Maritime Organization (IMO) to use new fuel consumption data to reassess and recalibrate the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) reference lines. items.title: IMO launches survey on Maritime Single Windows
items.summary: The IMO has launched a survey with the view to gathering information on the level of implementation and use of Maritime Single Window (MSW) systems to better understand the impact of MSW implementation on the administrative workload of maritime stakeholders and users.

items.title: Tripartite 2026 focuses on practical steps towards the next generation of ships
items.summary: Regulatory clarity, decarbonisation and digitalisation were central to discussions as more than 85 representatives of shipbuilders, shipowners and classification societies, together with invited observers, met in Tokyo on 28–29 October for Tripartite 2026. items.title: Preventing engine room fires before small defects become emergencies
items.summary:
BIMCO’s Tanker Safety Network recently examined how leaking pipes, inadequate insulation and electrical faults can develop into serious fires.
Members shared practical experience and discussed the maintenance, technology and organisational support needed to reduce the risk.

items.title: New industry frameworks set out to cut duplicated emissions reporting
items.summary: Two voluntary frameworks released today by a BIMCO-chaired industry working group give shipowners and operators a common way to share vessel operational and emissions data, so the same information no longer has to be mapped, entered and checked several times over.

items.title: Ballast Water: BIMCO seeks clearer guidance for ships facing challenging water quality
items.summary:
We have co-sponsored a submission to MEPC 85 making the case for revising the IMO guidance related to ballast water management for ships operating in challenging water quality conditions.

items.title: An opportunity to contribute your thoughts on plastic waste management
items.summary:
As part of our collaboration with the Maritime Association for Clean Seas (MACS), we are pleased to share information about an upcoming virtual round table on plastic waste management.
BIMCO members are therefore invited to attend and contribute practical operational experience.

items.title: BIMCO Energy Saving Device Retrofit Addendum available to support vessel efficiency investments
items.summary:

items.title: We have updated RECYCLECON – the global standard contract for sustainable ship recycling
items.summary:
The update reflects the entry into force of the Hong Kong Convention last year, as well as significant developments in ship recycling practice, regulatory requirements and sale and purchase procedures.

items.title: eBL adoption passes halfway mark
items.summary:
Electronic bill of lading (eBL) adoption has reached 51.1%, according to the FIT Alliance’s 2026 global survey, up from 49.2% in 2024 and 33% in 2022.
BIMCO is a founding member of the alliance.

items.summary:

items.summary:
